subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a default subagent tool-inactivity watchdog with nudge then abort semantics, or should this stay blocked behind the broader session activity/watchdog/manual-control design?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow repair: it adds new config/default behavior, automatic kill policy, model-visible injected messages, and user-visible channel recovery semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Core Subagent Recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open as the subagent-specific product slice and define guarded defaults, nudge copy, abort semantics, parent notification, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Depend On Activity API First
options.body: Keep the issue open but make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39127 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39141 prerequisites so recovery consumes a single activity/attention source.

options.title: Limit Core To Timeout And Manual Control
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge/kill defaults now; rely on runTimeoutSeconds and a separate manual kill/reap surface if maintainers decide automatic abort is too risky.

recommendation.title: Design Core Subagent Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the subagent-specific product slice and define guarded defaults, nudge copy, abort semantics, parent notification, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across subagent timeout enforcement, lifecycle handling, and recovery-sensitive runtime policy among the identified owners.
